rows.description: A young adult says that is a fair point and adjusts their position. Yielding to a good argument builds credibility and shows that the goal is truth, not ego.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: Partners or colleagues in a heated dispute agree to take twenty minutes and come back. A planned pause is not avoidance if it ends with a return to the matter.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A person whose partner goes silent, arms crossed, during a disagreement feels shut out and escalates. The silent one is often overwhelmed and needs a break, and both need a way to say so.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child reads a short okay from a friend as anger. Without voice and face, short messages get interpreted through the reader's own fears.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager notices a full stop after a reply or a missing emoji and worries a friend is upset. Tone in text is guessed, and guesses lean negative when anxious.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult asks are you upset with me or is it my imagination, instead of building a story from a delayed reply. Asking a direct, gentle question stops anxious spirals.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A person recognises a sensitive matter is escalating over messages and calls or meets in person. Voice and face carry warmth that text cannot.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A person sees a message read but not answered and starts spinning explanations. Delays usually mean busyness, and giving others the benefit of doubt saves needless pain.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: anxiety, doubt, hurt

rows.description: A teenager sends long voice notes to close friends, laughing and rambling. Voice notes feel more personal than text and carry emotion, but assume the friend has time and privacy.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student receives a five-minute voice note in a lecture or on a train and cannot listen. Receivers often want a text summary, and senders may not realise the demand on their time.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26
